ai.definition: RAG Pipelines refer to a technology that integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods, combining the strengths of retrieval-based and generative models to improve efficiency and accuracy in information processing.
ai.howItWorks: These pipelines work by first retrieving relevant documents or passages from a database using a retrieval model. Then, a generative model is used to refine and expand this retrieved content into more detailed or coherent responses. This approach leverages the speed and precision of retrieval models with the creativity and context understanding of generative models.
ai.problemSolved: The technology addresses the limitations of purely generative models in terms of accuracy and efficiency, as well as the limitations of pure retrieval systems in generating new content.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves developing and training both retrieval and generative models. This requires significant computational resources and expertise in natural language processing (NLP) techniques.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes data collection, model selection, training, fine-tuning, and validation steps. The pipeline is then tested for performance metrics such as recall, precision, and generation quality before deployment.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the computational resources required for model training, the cost of maintaining large datasets, and the expertise needed to develop and refine the models.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as RAG pipelines show promise in various applications such as customer service chatbots, knowledge base systems, and content generation tools. However, challenges remain in scaling and maintaining model performance over time.
ai.regulation: Regulations may vary by jurisdiction but will likely focus on data privacy, bias mitigation, and transparency of AI decision-making processes.
ai.profitability: Profitability is dependent on the specific application but shows potential for cost savings and improved service through more accurate and efficient information retrieval.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include improvements in model efficiency, better handling of long-tail queries, and enhanced integration with other AI technologies like knowledge graphs and semantic search.

glossary.def: A technology combining retrieval and generative models to improve information processing efficiency and accuracy.
A method that integrates retrieval-based models with generative models for improved AI capabilities in text processing.

subsystems.name: Ingestion and parsing
subsystems.role: turn messy source files into clean text a machine can index.
parts: connectors to document stores, wikis, databases

subsystems.name: Chunking and enrichment
subsystems.role: cut documents into retrievable passages that still carry meaning.
parts: optional summaries or synthetic questions per chunk

subsystems.name: Embedding and indexing
subsystems.role: store passages so similar meanings can be found quickly.
parts: approximate nearest-neighbour index (e.g. HNSW or IVF-PQ)

subsystems.name: Query processing
subsystems.role: improve the raw user question before it hits the index.
parts: hybrid fusion of dense and keyword results

subsystems.name: Retrieval and reranking
subsystems.role: pick the few passages that actually help, out of thousands of candidates.

subsystems.name: Context assembly and generation
subsystems.role: pack the evidence into a prompt and produce a grounded answer.
parts: prompt template with instructions and citations

subsystems.name: Evaluation and monitoring
subsystems.role: prove the pipeline is accurate and catch it drifting.

buildSteps.title: Collect the corpus
buildSteps.detail: Decide which documents the system may answer from, and connect to those sources. Permissions matter: a user must never retrieve a passage they are not allowed to read.

buildSteps.title: Parse to clean text
buildSteps.detail: Extract text from PDFs, web pages and databases, recover headings and tables, and strip boilerplate such as navigation and footers.

buildSteps.title: Chunk the text
buildSteps.detail: Split each document into passages of a few hundred tokens with some overlap, so a sentence split across a boundary is still retrievable.

buildSteps.title: Enrich with metadata
buildSteps.detail: Attach source, date, section and access tags to every chunk, and optionally generate a short summary or question that the chunk answers.

buildSteps.title: Embed and index
buildSteps.detail: Run each chunk through an embedding model and write the vectors into an approximate nearest-neighbour index; build a keyword index over the same chunks for exact-term matching.

buildSteps.title: Build the query pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Add rewriting, expansion and hybrid fusion so that vague, conversational or acronym-heavy questions still retrieve well.

buildSteps.title: Add retrieval and reranking
buildSteps.detail: Fetch a generous candidate set, rerank it with a more accurate (and slower) model, then keep the best handful within the token budget.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and generate
buildSteps.detail: Insert the chosen passages into a prompt that instructs the model to answer only from them and to cite each claim.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and operate
buildSteps.detail: Measure retrieval and answer quality on a held-out question set, then re-index as sources change and monitor for degraded or hallucinated answers.

prerequisites.why: both the embedding models and the generator depend on them; the technique was first described in a 2020 research paper.
exact nearest-neighbour search is too slow over millions of chunks, so approximate indexes are essential.
several retrieved passages must fit in the prompt alongside the conversation and instructions.
retrieval plus generation multiplies cost and latency, so serving economics decide what is practical.
detecting unsupported claims automatically is still imperfect, which limits how much autonomy can be given to the system.

pathway.milestone: production RAG over enterprise document sets with citations
pathway.unlocks: question answering that reflects private, changing data without retraining the model.

pathway.milestone: hybrid search, rerankers and multi-step or agentic retrieval as defaults
pathway.unlocks: handling of comparative, multi-hop and numeric questions that a single search pass gets wrong.

pathway.milestone: graph and structured retrieval over entities and relationships
pathway.unlocks: answers that require joining facts rather than quoting one passage.

pathway.milestone: retrieval trained into the model or triggered during generation
pathway.unlocks: lower latency and fewer missed passages, with verifiable citations as the standard.
